preamble: A rhotic [r] becomes the voiceless stop [t] by total assimilation to an adjacent [t]. The classic case is the Middle Indo-Aryan simplification of Sanskrit clusters: in Pali the r of -tr- and -rt- is absorbed by the stop, giving a geminate -tt- (Sanskrit putra > Pali putta 'son', sūtra > sutta 'thread; discourse'). Outside such clusters a direct change of a trill to a stop is not well attested.

examples.note: Progressive assimilation of r to the preceding t in the cluster -tr-, giving a geminate.
Same assimilation of -tr- to -tt-, with the long vowel shortened before the geminate.
